correctness.rationale: For each output edge, harmonic-measure difference nu is a zero-mass leaf signed measure; telescoping along root-to-leaf paths gives its exact dual edge-Lipschitz norm as sum over cuts |nu(C_e)|. The sign of each cut is realizable by a tree potential (acyclicity), hence not merely an upper bound. For non-path trees, leaf-distance witness g=d(a,.) gives Lg=2-deg<=0; w=H(g|leaves)-g solves Lw=deg-2>=0 with positive source at a branch and zero on boundary, so strict maximum principle yields w>0 inside, forcing an edge slope >1. On paths affine interpolation is norm one. On spiders, center is conductance-weighted by inverse arm lengths; directly bound output slope by 1+(m-2)/(L_i sum 1/L_j), exact with distance-from-shortest-leaf boundary data; simultaneous triangle-equality saturation gives all norming data. Shortening a minimum arm to one reduces denominator, and reciprocal convexity balances others for fixed n,m. AM/HM lower bound and balanced witnesses give (1/2+o(1))sqrt(n) and strict 1+sqrt(n-2)/2 upper bound. Exact rational verification source read and bounded independent reasoning; previous code tests are finite only.
